scheme_name: Widowed Parent's Allowance
description: Government support scheme in the United Kingdom: Widowed Parent's Allowance.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be widowed, meaning their spouse or civil partner has died.

2. Applicant must have been married to or in a civil partnership with the deceased person at the time of death.

3. Applicant must be under State Pension age.

4. Applicant must be entitled to Child Benefit for at least one qualifying child, or have been pregnant when their spouse or civil partner died.

5. The deceased spouse or civil partner must have paid sufficient National Insurance contributions or died as a result of an industrial accident or disease.

6. Applicant must not have remarried or entered into a new civil partnership.

7. Applicant must satisfy all eligibility requirements established by the UK Department for Work and Pensions (DWP).

8. Applicant must reside in the United Kingdom or otherwise satisfy the residence requirements applicable to Widowed Parent's Allowance.
benefits: Financial assistance, support services, grants, allowances, or statutory benefits as applicable under the scheme.
required_documents: your partner paidNational Insurance contributions, or they died because of an accident at work or a disease caused by work
you’re entitled toChild Benefitfor at least one child

scheme_name: Winter Fuel Payment
description: Government support scheme in the United Kingdom: Winter Fuel Payment.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must have been born on or before 27 June 1960.

2. Applicant must usually live in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland.

3. Applicant must satisfy the residency requirements during the qualifying week specified by the government.

4. Applicants who usually live outside England, Wales, or Northern Ireland are not eligible.

5. Applicants who were in prison for the entire qualifying week are not eligible.

6. Applicants whose immigration status prohibits access to public funds are not eligible.

7. Applicants who received free hospital treatment for the entire qualifying week and the corresponding period in the previous year may not be eligible.

8. Applicants living in a care home may be eligible; however, those who receive Universal Credit, Pension Credit, or income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) and have lived in a care home continuously since 28 June 2026 or earlier are not eligible.

9. Applicant must satisfy all eligibility conditions established by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP).
benefits: Financial assistance, support services, grants, allowances, or statutory benefits as applicable under the scheme.
required_documents: you get Universal Credit, Pension Credit or income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
you lived in a care home for the whole time from 28 June 2026 or earlier

scheme_name: Your benefits, tax and pension after the death of a partner
description: Government support scheme in the United Kingdom: Your benefits, tax and pension after the death of a partner.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a surviving spouse, civil partner, or widow/widower whose husband, wife, or civil partner has died.

2. Applicant must be receiving or expecting changes in income, pensions, benefits, allowances, or inheritance following the death of their partner.

3. Applicant may be eligible for adjustments to tax allowances, including Personal Allowance, Married Couple's Allowance, or Blind Person's Allowance, subject to HMRC rules.

4. Applicant may be required to notify HMRC of changes in taxable income resulting from pensions, benefits, investments, rental income, annuities, or other sources.

5. Widows married before April 1977 may be eligible to continue paying a reduced rate of National Insurance, subject to HMRC eligibility requirements.

6. Applicant must satisfy all HMRC requirements relating to tax, National Insurance, and survivor-related benefits and allowances.

7. Applicant must be resident in the United Kingdom and subject to UK tax regulations.
benefits: Financial assistance, support services, grants, allowances, or statutory benefits as applicable under the scheme.
required_documents: Winter Fuel Payment- if you were born on or before 5 July 1952
Cold Weather Payment- if you’re on a low income

scheme_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
description: Provides nutrition benefits to supplement the food budget of needy families so they can purchase healthy food and move towards self-sufficiency.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a resident of the United States.

2. Applicant must belong to a low-income household and meet the income requirements specified by the state SNAP agency.

3. Applicant must satisfy the resource and asset limits prescribed by the state, including eligible bank account balances and other countable resources.

4. Applicant must meet all federal and state SNAP eligibility requirements.

5. Applicant may be required to complete an eligibility interview before approval.

6. Benefits are provided to eligible individuals and families to purchase food through an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card.
benefits: Monthly electronic benefits transferred to EBT card for grocery purchases.

scheme_name: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)
description: Safeguards the health of low-income pregnant, breastfeeding, and non-breastfeeding postpartum women and infants and children up to age 5.
eligibility_text: Pregnant, recently pregnant, or breastfeeding women; infants; children up to 5 years old who meet income and nutrition risk criteria.
benefits: Nutritious foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals.

scheme_name: National School Lunch Program
description: A federally assisted meal program operating in public and nonprofit private schools and residential child care institutions.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a school-age child enrolled in a participating school under the National School Lunch Program (NSLP).

2. Children from households with income at or below 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) are eligible for free school meals.

3. Children from households with income between 130% and 185% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) are eligible for reduced-price school meals.

4. Children belonging to low-income households may qualify based on household income and household size.

5. Children whose households receive SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR benefits are automatically eligible for free school meals.

6. Foster children, homeless children, migrant children, runaway children, and Head Start participants are categorically eligible for free school meals.

7. Eligibility may be determined through a household application or through automatic certification based on participation in qualifying federal assistance programs.

8. Applicant must satisfy all federal and state program requirements established under the National School Lunch Program.
benefits: Low-cost or free lunches to children each school day.

scheme_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
description: Provides nutritious meals and snacks to children and adults who receive care in eligible non-residential day care settings.
eligibility_text:
1. Children aged 12 years or younger enrolled in participating child care centers, family day care homes, Head Start programs, after-school care programs, or emergency shelters are eligible.

2. Migrant children and children residing in emergency shelters may be eligible regardless of age restrictions applicable to other children.

3. Adults aged 60 years or older receiving care in participating adult day care centers are eligible.

4. Adults with disabilities enrolled in participating adult day care centers are eligible regardless of age.

5. Applicants must be enrolled in a facility approved to participate in the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP).

6. Eligibility may also be determined based on household income or participation in qualifying assistance programs.

7. Applicants must reside in the United States and satisfy all federal and state CACFP requirements.
benefits: Reimbursement for nutritious meals and snacks to participating providers.

scheme_name: Summer Food Service Program (SFSP)
description: Ensures that low-income children continue to receive nutritious meals during summer months when school is not in session.
eligibility_text: Children 18 years and under in low-income areas; disabled persons over 18.
benefits: Free, nutritious meals during summer months.

scheme_name: Medicaid
description: A joint federal and state program that helps with medical costs for some people with limited income and resources.
eligibility_text: Low-income adults, children, pregnant women, elderly adults, and people with disabilities.
benefits: Comprehensive health coverage including doctor visits, hospital stays, and medications.

scheme_name: Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)
description: Provides health coverage to eligible children through both Medicaid and separate CHIP programs.
eligibility_text: Children up to age 19 whose families earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance.
benefits: Routine check-ups, immunizations, doctor visits, prescriptions, dental and vision care.

scheme_name: Medicare
description: Federal health insurance program for people 65 or older, certain younger people with disabilities, and people with End-Stage Renal Disease.
eligibility_text: U.S. citizens or permanent residents 65+ years old; certain disabled individuals.
benefits: Hospital insurance (Part A), medical insurance (Part B), prescription drug coverage (Part D).

scheme_name: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program
description: Provides a comprehensive system of care for low-income people with HIV.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be diagnosed with HIV/AIDS and require HIV-related medical care, treatment, medications, or support services.

2. Applicant must be a resident of the United States and meet the residency requirements of the state or territory administering the program.

3. Applicant must be uninsured, underinsured, or unable to adequately afford HIV-related healthcare services through other available resources.

4. Applicant must meet the income eligibility requirements established by the state, territory, or local Ryan White program provider, which are generally based on a percentage of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL).

5. Applicant may be required to provide proof of HIV diagnosis, proof of residence, proof of income, and identification documents during enrollment and recertification.

6. Applicant must utilize available third-party payment sources, including private insurance, Medicare, or Medicaid, before receiving Ryan White-funded assistance, as the program serves as a payer of last resort.

7. Low-income individuals living with HIV/AIDS are given priority for Ryan White-funded medical care, medications, and support services.

8. Eligibility determination and continued participation are subject to the requirements established by the state, territory, local Ryan White program, or service provider.
benefits: Medical care, treatment, essential support services, and medications.

scheme_name: Indian Health Service (IHS)
description: Provides a comprehensive health services delivery system for American Indians and Alaska Natives.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a member of a federally recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native community.

2. Applicant must be eligible for services under the Indian Health Service (IHS) program as determined by federal law and IHS regulations.

3. American Indians and Alaska Natives who can establish tribal membership, descendant status, or other qualifying affiliation may be eligible for IHS-funded healthcare services.

4. Applicant may be required to provide documentation proving membership in a federally recognized tribe or eligibility through an eligible Alaska Native group.

5. There are no income-based eligibility requirements for receiving IHS services.

6. Eligible individuals must reside in the United States and meet applicable tribal and federal eligibility criteria.

7. Healthcare services are provided to eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives through IHS facilities, tribal health programs, and urban Indian health programs.

8. Eligibility determination is subject to verification of tribal affiliation and compliance with IHS program requirements.
benefits: Comprehensive health services including preventive care, hospital care, and community health.

scheme_name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program
description: Assists very low-income families, the elderly, and the disabled to afford decent, safe, and sanitary housing in the private market.
eligibility_text: Very low-income families, elderly, and disabled individuals.
benefits: Rental assistance vouchers covering difference between rent and 30% of household income.

scheme_name: Public Housing Program
description: HUD provides affordable public housing to eligible low-income families, the elderly, and people with disabilities.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a U.S. citizen or have eligible immigration status.

2. Applicant must belong to a low-income family, elderly household, or a person with disabilities as defined by the Public Housing Agency (PHA).

3. Household income must not exceed the income limits established by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), typically 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI).

4. Applicants with very low income (50% of AMI or below) may receive priority for housing assistance.

5. Applicant must provide accurate information regarding household composition, income, assets, and citizenship or immigration status.

6. Applicants must pass the screening requirements established by the local Public Housing Agency, which may include rental history, criminal background checks, and compliance with program rules.

7. Eligible households must reside in the United States and occupy the housing unit as their primary residence.

8. Eligibility determination is subject to verification of income, family status, and other requirements established by HUD and the local Public Housing Agency.
benefits: Decent and safe rental housing at reduced rates based on income.

scheme_name: HOME Investment Partnerships Program
description: The largest federal block grant to state and local governments designed exclusively to create affordable housing.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a resident of the United States.
2. Eligible beneficiary types — any one of the following:
   a. Homebuyer — gross household income must not exceed 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI) where the property is located.
   b. Renter or Tenant-Based Assistance — at least 90% of benefiting families must have incomes at or below 60% of the AMI. A portion of units must serve those earning 50% or less of the AMI.
3. Property requirements for homeownership or rehabilitation assistance:
   a. The home must serve as the owner's primary and principal residence.
   b. Estimated property value must not exceed 95% of the median area purchase price.
4. HOME-assisted homes are subject to resale or recapture provisions during the affordability period:
   a. If the property is sold before the affordability period expires, the owner must either preserve affordability for another low-income buyer or repay the HOME subsidy.
benefits: Affordable housing construction, rehabilitation, and homebuyer assistance.

scheme_name: Section 202 Supportive Housing for the Elderly
description: Provides funding to expand the supply of affordable housing with supportive services for the elderly.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a resident of the United States.
2. At least one household member must be 62 years of age or older.
3. Total household income must be 50% or less of the Area Median Income (AMI).
4. Priority is given to those classified as very low-income (around 30% of the AMI or less).
5. Applicant must demonstrate a need for supportive services to maintain independent living.
6. The value of household assets may be restricted and income generated from assets is factored into total household income.
benefits: Safe housing integrated with supportive services such as cleaning, transportation, meals.

scheme_name: Emergency Solutions Grants (ESG)
description: Provides funding to help people quickly regain stability in permanent housing after experiencing a housing crisis.
eligibility_text: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
benefits: Emergency shelter, rapid re-housing, homelessness prevention, and HMIS support.

scheme_name: Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)
description: Provides benefits to disabled or blind people who are insured by workers' contributions to the Social Security Trust Fund.
eligibility_text: Workers who have paid Social Security taxes and have a qualifying disability.
benefits: Monthly cash benefits; Medicare eligibility after 24 months.

scheme_name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
description: Pays benefits to disabled adults and children who have limited income and resources.
eligibility_text: Disabled, blind, or 65+ adults and disabled children with limited income.
benefits: Monthly cash payment to meet basic needs (food, clothing, shelter).

scheme_name: Ticket to Work Program
description: Helps Social Security disability beneficiaries age 18–64 who want to work go to work.
eligibility_text: SSDI or SSI beneficiaries aged 18–64 who want to return to work.
benefits: Employment support services, vocational rehabilitation, and continued benefits during transition.

scheme_name: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Tax Credits
description: Provides tax credits and deductions for businesses that make themselves accessible to persons with disabilities.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a small business that incurs eligible expenses to improve accessibility for persons with disabilities.

2. Businesses must comply with the accessibility requirements established under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

3. Eligible expenses may include costs related to removing architectural, communication, physical, or transportation barriers for individuals with disabilities.

4. Small businesses with gross receipts of $1 million or less in the previous tax year, or with no more than 30 full-time employees, may qualify for the Disabled Access Credit.

5. Businesses making accessibility-related modifications or accommodations for customers or employees with disabilities may be eligible for tax benefits.

6. Applicant must maintain records and documentation supporting qualified accessibility expenditures.

7. Tax credits and deductions are available only for qualifying accessibility improvements and are subject to IRS regulations.

8. Applicant must operate within the United States and comply with all applicable federal tax requirements.
benefits: Disabled Access Credit; Architectural Barrier Removal Deduction.

scheme_name: VA Disability Compensation
description: A tax-free monetary benefit paid to Veterans with disabilities that are the result of a disease or injury incurred or aggravated during active military service.
eligibility_text: Veterans with service-connected disabilities.
benefits: Monthly tax-free compensation based on disability rating (10–100%).

scheme_name: VA Home Loan Guaranty
description: Helps Servicemembers, Veterans, and eligible surviving spouses become homeowners.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a U.S. military Veteran, Active-Duty Service Member, National Guard Member, Reservist, or an eligible Surviving Spouse.

2. Applicant must satisfy the minimum military service requirements established by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

3. Applicant must obtain a valid Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from the VA.

4. Applicant must meet the credit and income requirements of the participating lender.

5. The property being financed must generally be used as the applicant's primary residence.

6. Eligible surviving spouses of service members who died in service or as a result of a service-connected disability may qualify.

7. Applicant must comply with all VA and lender-specific loan requirements.

8. Applicant must be a resident of the United States and eligible under VA Home Loan Guaranty guidelines.
benefits: No down payment required; no private mortgage insurance; competitive interest rates.

scheme_name: Montgomery GI Bill — Active Duty (MGIB-AD)
description: Provides up to 36 months of education benefits for Veterans who served on active duty.
eligibility_text: Veterans with at least 2 years of active duty service.
benefits: Provides up to 36 months of education benefits for Veterans who served on active duty.

scheme_name: Veterans Pension
description: A needs-based benefit paid to wartime Veterans with low income who are no longer able to work.
eligibility_text: Wartime Veterans with low income who are permanently disabled or aged 65+.
benefits: Monthly pension payments based on income and medical expenses.

scheme_name: VA Caregiver Support Program
description: Provides resources, education, and financial support to family caregivers of eligible Veterans.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a resident of the United States.

2. VETERAN ELIGIBILITY:
   a. Must have served in the active military, naval, or air service.
   b. Must have been discharged under conditions other than dishonorable.
   c. Must have a single or combined service-connected disability rating of 70% or more from the VA.
   d. Must require in-person personal care services for a minimum of 6 continuous months — defined as needing help with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) or needing supervision or protection due to neurological or mental health impairments.

3. PRIMARY FAMILY CAREGIVER ELIGIBILITY:
   a. Must be at least 18 years of age.
   b. Must be one of the following — spouse, son, daughter, parent, step-family member, extended family member, or a person who lives with the veteran full-time.
   c. Must be capable of providing safe and effective care.
   d. Must pass a background check.
   e. Must complete the required VA caregiver education and training programme.
benefits: Monthly stipend, health insurance, respite care, mental health services.

scheme_name: Federal Pell Grant
description: Need-based grants to low-income undergraduate and certain post-baccalaureate students to promote access to postsecondary education.
eligibility_text: Undergraduate students with financial need who have not earned a bachelor's degree.
benefits: Grants up to $7,395/year (2024–25) that do not need to be repaid.

scheme_name: Federal Work-Study (FWS)
description: Provides part-time employment opportunities to undergraduate and graduate students with financial need.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a student enrolled or accepted for enrollment in an eligible undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at a participating institution.

2. Applicant must demonstrate financial need as determined through the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).

3. Applicant must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or eligible non-citizen and satisfy federal student aid eligibility requirements.

4. Applicant must maintain satisfactory academic progress according to the standards established by the educational institution.

5. Applicant must be enrolled at least part-time if required by the institution's Federal Work-Study policies.

6. Employment opportunities provided through the program may be on-campus, off-campus, or with approved community service organizations.

7. Priority for Federal Work-Study funding may be given to students with exceptional financial need.

8. Applicant must comply with all institutional and federal requirements governing participation in the Federal Work-Study Program.
benefits: Part-time employment earnings to help pay education expenses.

scheme_name: Teacher Education Assistance for College and Higher Education (TEACH) Grant
description: Provides grants of up to $4,000 per year to students who intend to teach full-time in a high-need field at a low-income school.
eligibility_text: Students planning to teach in high-need subjects at schools serving low-income students.
benefits: Up to $4,000/year in grant funding; converts to loan if teaching obligation not met.
documents_required: FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid)
Course completion verification for high-need subjects
required_documents: FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid)
Course completion verification for high-need subjects

scheme_name: Head Start Program
description: Promotes the school readiness of young children from low-income families through education, health, social, and other services.
eligibility_text: Children from birth to age 5 from low-income families.
benefits: Comprehensive early childhood education, health, and nutrition services.

scheme_name: 21st Century Community Learning Centers
description: Provides before- and after-school programs, summer programs, and other out-of-school activities for students in high-poverty, low-performing schools.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a student attending a school that participates in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) program.

2. Priority is given to students attending high-poverty and low-performing schools identified as needing academic support and enrichment opportunities.

3. Students must participate in eligible before-school, after-school, summer, or extended-learning programs operated under a 21st CCLC grant.

4. The program primarily serves students from low-income families and communities with significant educational needs.

5. Academic enrichment activities, tutoring, homework assistance, STEM education, arts, technology, and youth development services are provided to eligible students.

6. Family members of participating students may also be eligible for certain family literacy and educational support activities offered through the program.

7. Applicant must meet the enrollment and participation requirements established by the local 21st CCLC program provider.

8. Applicant must reside in the United States and attend an eligible participating school.
benefits: Academic enrichment, tutoring, career/technical education programs.

scheme_name: Unemployment Insurance (UI)
description: Provides temporary financial assistance to eligible workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own.
eligibility_text: Workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own and meet state eligibility criteria.
benefits: Weekly cash benefits typically lasting up to 26 weeks.

scheme_name: Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA)
description: Provides aid to workers who have lost their jobs or suffered a reduction in hours and wages as a result of increased imports.
eligibility_text: Workers displaced by foreign trade competition.
benefits: Training, job search allowances, relocation allowances, and income support.

scheme_name: Job Corps
description: The nation's largest free residential education and job training program for young people.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a young person seeking education, vocational training, employment skills, or career development opportunities.

2. Applicant must generally be between 16 and 24 years of age at the time of enrollment.

3. Applicant must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, refugee, asylee, or otherwise authorized to work in the United States.

4. Applicant must meet low-income eligibility requirements established under the Job Corps program.

5. Applicant must require additional education, vocational training, counseling, or employment assistance to successfully enter the workforce.

6. Applicant must be free from serious behavioral issues that would prevent participation in a residential training environment.

7. Applicant must demonstrate the ability and willingness to participate fully in the Job Corps educational and career training program.

8. Applicant must satisfy all enrollment and eligibility requirements established by the U.S. Department of Labor and Job Corps program administrators.
benefits: Career technical training, high school diploma/GED, job placement assistance.

scheme_name: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Adult Program
description: Provides job training and other services to help adults enter or re-enter the workforce.
eligibility_text: Adults age 18 and older seeking employment or better jobs.
benefits: Career counseling, job training, resume help, job placement services.

scheme_name: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
description: A refundable federal tax credit for low- to moderate-income workers and families, particularly those with children.
eligibility_text: Low- to moderate-income workers meeting income and filing requirements.
benefits: Refundable tax credit up to $7,430 depending on income and number of children.

scheme_name: Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF)
description: Provides financial assistance for child care to low-income families to support parental employment, training, or education.
eligibility_text: Low-income families with children under age 13.
benefits: Provides financial assistance for child care to low-income families to support parental employment, training, or education.

scheme_name: Child Tax Credit (CTC)
description: A tax credit for families with qualifying children to help offset the costs of raising children.
eligibility_text: Families with qualifying children under age 17.
benefits: Up to $2,000 per qualifying child; up to $1,600 refundable.

scheme_name: Adoption Assistance Program
description: Provides financial and medical assistance to adoptive families who adopt children with special needs from foster care.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be an adoptive parent or prospective adoptive parent of a child determined to have special needs.

2. The child must be legally eligible for adoption and placement through a public child welfare agency or an authorized adoption agency.

3. The child must be unable to return safely to the birth parents and must require adoption as a permanent placement option.

4. The child must meet the state's definition of a special needs child, which may include age, membership in a sibling group, medical condition, physical disability, mental disability, emotional condition, or other factors that make adoption more difficult.

5. Reasonable efforts must have been made to place the child without adoption assistance, except where such efforts are not in the child's best interests.

6. An adoption assistance agreement must be signed between the adoptive parents and the responsible state agency before the adoption is finalized.

7. The child must be a U.S. citizen, qualified non-citizen, or otherwise eligible under federal and state adoption assistance requirements.

8. Applicants must satisfy all state and federal requirements governing adoption assistance benefits.
benefits: Adoption subsidy payments, Medicaid coverage, and nonrecurring adoption expenses.

scheme_name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF)
description: Provides temporary financial assistance and work opportunities to needy families.
eligibility_text: Low-income families with children under 18.
benefits: Cash assistance, job training, child care, and transportation support.

scheme_name: Foster Care Program (Title IV-E)
description: Provides federal funding to states to pay the costs of foster care for children who would otherwise remain in an unsafe home.
eligibility_text: Children removed from their homes due to abuse or neglect.
benefits: Foster care maintenance payments, case management, and supportive services.

scheme_name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
description: Assists low-income households with their energy costs — particularly heating and cooling bills.
eligibility_text: Low-income households, especially those with elderly, disabled members, or young children.
benefits: Home heating and cooling assistance; energy crisis assistance.

scheme_name: Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
description: Reduces energy costs for low-income families by improving the energy efficiency of their homes.
eligibility_text: Low-income households, especially elderly, disabled, and families with young children.
benefits: Energy efficiency upgrades (insulation, air sealing, HVAC improvements) at no cost.

scheme_name: Social Security Retirement Benefits
description: Monthly benefits for qualified retired workers and their dependents based on the worker's lifetime earnings.
eligibility_text: Workers age 62+ who have earned sufficient Social Security credits.
benefits: Monthly retirement benefit; Medicare eligibility at 65.

scheme_name: Social Security Survivor Benefits
description: Provides income to families of deceased insured workers.
eligibility_text:
1. Applicant must be a surviving family member of a deceased worker who earned sufficient Social Security credits through employment.

2. Surviving spouse may be eligible if aged 60 years or older, or 50 years or older if disabled.

3. Surviving spouse caring for the deceased worker's child who is under age 16 or disabled may be eligible regardless of age.

4. Unmarried children of the deceased worker may be eligible if they are under 18 years of age, or under 19 years of age and attending elementary or secondary school full-time.

5. Adult children may be eligible if they have a qualifying disability that began before age 22.

6. Dependent parents of the deceased worker may be eligible if they are aged 62 years or older and received substantial support from the deceased worker.

7. Applicant must meet all relationship, age, disability, dependency, and documentation requirements established by the Social Security Administration (SSA).

8. Applicant must reside in the United States or otherwise satisfy Social Security survivor benefit eligibility requirements.
benefits: Monthly survivor benefits based on deceased worker's earnings record.
documents_required: Birth Certificate (for children and dependent parents)
required_documents: Birth Certificate (for children and dependent parents)

scheme_name: General Assistance (GA)
description: State and locally funded cash assistance programs for individuals who do not qualify for federally funded programs.
eligibility_text: Low-income individuals who do not qualify for federal programs.
benefits: Cash assistance and referral services; varies by state.

scheme_name: Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit
description: A non-refundable credit for expenses paid for the care of a qualifying child or dependent, enabling the taxpayer to work.
eligibility_text: Working parents or individuals paying for dependent care.
benefits: Up to $3,000 for one dependent or $6,000 for two or more dependents in care expenses.

scheme_name: American Opportunity Tax Credit (AOTC)
description: A credit for qualified education expenses paid for an eligible student for the first four years of higher education.
eligibility_text: Students in first 4 years of higher education.
benefits: Up to $2,500 per eligible student; 40% (up to $1,000) is refundable.

scheme_name: Lifetime Learning Credit
description: A tax credit for qualified tuition and fees paid for eligible students at educational institutions.
eligibility_text: Students taking courses to acquire or improve job skills; no limit on years.
benefits: Up to $2,000 per tax return (20% of first $10,000 of qualified expenses).

scheme_name: Older Americans Act Nutrition Program
description: Provides congregate and home-delivered meals and other nutrition services to older adults.
eligibility_text: Adults aged 60 and older (no income requirement).
benefits: Congregate meals at senior centers; home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels).

scheme_name: Senior Community Service Employment Program (SCSEP)
description: Provides subsidized part-time employment and job training for low-income adults aged 55 and older.
eligibility_text: Low-income individuals aged 55+ who are unemployed.
benefits: Part-time paid community service jobs; job search assistance.

scheme_name: Medicare Savings Programs (MSPs)
description: Help pay Medicare premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance for low-income Medicare beneficiaries.
eligibility_text: Medicare beneficiaries with limited income and resources.
benefits: Help paying Medicare Part A and B premiums, deductibles, and cost-sharing.
